title: Millions remember something that never was

lines.text: Millions of people remember things that never happened. The same wrong memory, shared by strangers.
Researcher Fiona Broome named it after remembering Nelson Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s.
He actually died in 2013, years after becoming president.
And hundreds of people said they remembered it too.
Do you remember the Berenstein Bears? It was always Berenstain.
Darth Vader never said, Luke, I am your father. He said, No, I am your father.
And Mr Monopoly has never worn a monocle.
Psychologists think shared false memories come from shared assumptions. But some people insist reality changed.

sources.claim: Mandela effect named by Fiona Broome after a false memory of Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s (he died in 2013); examples: Berenstain Bears, 'No, I am your father', Mr Monopoly's monocle
Prasad & Bainbridge (2022) on the visual Mandela effect as shared false memories

publish.title: Millions Remember Things That Never Happened 🌀
publish.description: Berenstain, not Berenstein. 'No, I am your father.' No monocle. The Mandela effect explained.
